title: Interactive Evidence Maps for Visualizing and Understanding Systematic Reviews
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a methodological problem in research synthesis: systematic reviews and meta-analyses often provide only static tables, figures, and narrative summaries, which can obscure study-level detail, overgeneralize findings, and make it difficult for readers to explore evidence in ways that match their own questions. The authors propose interactive evidence maps as a way to make systematic review data more transparent, explorable, and analytically flexible.

The approach combines large language model-based topic modeling with interactive visualization. Review data that have already been systematically coded are uploaded in structured form, then an LLM (Claude) is prompted to identify topics and subtopics from study titles and abstracts. These topics are linked back to the original coded variables and displayed in an interactive interface built with D3.js and React, allowing filtering by topic and by coded study features such as year, methodology, educational level, and outcome type. The paper is therefore a framework/proof-of-concept rather than a primary intervention study.

To demonstrate the tool, the authors use data from a published scoping review of 112 studies on pedagogical agents in K-12 education. The dataset includes studies involving primary, lower secondary, and upper secondary learners, with topics such as science, mathematics, language, and social skills. The paper concludes that interactive evidence maps can complement traditional review reporting by revealing patterns, research gaps, and temporal shifts that are hard to detect in static summaries, while also improving transparency and supporting exploratory analysis. The authors also note several open concerns, including scalability, reproducibility, probabilistic assignment transparency, and the instability of LLM-generated topic labels.

identified_tools.name: Claude
identified_tools.description: Anthropic's large language model / conversational AI assistant used for prompt-based topic extraction and labeling from structured review data.
identified_tools.use_case: Used in the proof-of-concept pipeline to analyze coded study data and identify 6-8 main topics and 2-3 subtopics for each, assigning each study to a topic based on semantic similarity.

quality_tier_rationale: This paper is a proof-of-concept methods paper about interactive evidence maps, not an empirical evaluation of student outcomes or a controlled study of the AI tool itself. It reports implementation considerations and limitations rather than quantitative effectiveness evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests the tool may improve transparency, exploration, and identification of patterns and gaps in reviews, but it does not report outcome effect sizes on learners or classrooms. The impact is therefore promising but indirect and unquantified.
